result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO – March 2026 revenue recognition: Dunmore Foods and Harlow Freight (US entity)
Prepared by: Senior Accountant, 2026-04-03

ENTRIES POSTED (both dated 2026-03-31, US/USD, each under the USD 10,000 approval threshold – no controller approval required)

1. JE-00311 – Dunmore Foods, USD 5,000: Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue / Cr 4000 Subscription Revenue
   Support attached: DOC-0002 (Subscription Agreement), DOC-0155 (Amendment No. 1), DOC-0005 (INV-1001), DOC-0156 (INV-1052)
2. JE-00312 – Harlow Freight, USD 5,000: Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue
   Support attached: DOC-0001 (Usage Agreement), DOC-0206 (March 2026 usage report)

REASONING

Dunmore Foods – contract modification (ASC 606-10-25-10 to 25-13)
- Original contract: core platform subscription, USD 48,000 for 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, invoiced in advance (INV-1001, booked to deferred revenue in JE-00012; cash received JE-00079). Service is provided evenly over the term → a series/stand-ready obligation recognized ratably: 48,000/12 = USD 4,000 per month. Jan and Feb releases of 4,000 each are already posted (JE-00111, JE-00215).
- Amendment No. 1 (effective 2026-03-01) adds the Analytics module for 2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31 at USD 1,000/month (USD 10,000), invoiced in advance (INV-1052, booked to deferred revenue in JE-00229). The amendment explicitly states the module is a DISTINCT service priced at its STANDALONE SELLING PRICE. Both criteria of ASC 606-10-25-12 are met, so the modification is accounted for as a SEPARATE CONTRACT. Consequence: no reallocation of the original USD 48,000 transaction price and no cumulative catch-up; the core subscription continues at 4,000/month and the analytics module is recognized ratably over its own 10-month term at 10,000/10 = USD 1,000 per month.
- March recognition: 4,000 (core) + 1,000 (analytics) = USD 5,000, released from 2200. Both components were invoiced in advance, so the offset is deferred revenue (not A/R or unbilled).
- Rejected alternative: treating the amendment as a modification of the existing contract (blended rate of (36,000 remaining + 10,000)/10 = 4,600/month plus the core would have been misstated). That treatment applies only when the added services are NOT priced at SSP or are not distinct; the amendment documents both, so it does not apply.
- Post-entry check: 2200 ending balance USD 45,000 credit = 9 months × 4,000 core (36,000) + 9 months × 1,000 analytics (9,000). Ties exactly.

Harlow Freight – usage-based revenue (ASC 606-10-55-65 sales/usage-based fees; 606-10-55-18 'right to invoice' practical expedient)
- Contract: USD 0.10 per shipment, no minimum, performance obligation satisfied as each shipment is processed; usage billed quarterly in arrears with the Q1 invoice issued in early April.
- March usage report (DOC-0206): 50,000 shipments × 0.10 = USD 5,000. Only one March usage report exists; it is consistent with the Jan (41,200 → 4,120, JE-00112) and Feb (44,800 → 4,480, JE-00210) pattern.
- Because the revenue is earned in March but not yet invoiced, it is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables per policy §6, not to 1100 A/R. Usage-based fees are recognized when the usage occurs (variable consideration allocated entirely to the period of usage), so no constraint or estimation is needed – the amount is fixed by the actual count.
- Post-entry check: 1300 ending balance USD 13,600 = 4,120 + 4,480 + 5,000 = full Q1 usage. This should be reclassified to 1100 A/R when the Q1 invoice is issued in April; A/R team should be reminded to clear 1300 on invoicing rather than double-booking revenue.

OTHER CHECKS PERFORMED
- No SLA credits, uptime reports, customer emails or amendments affecting either customer in March were found in the document store (policy §7 credit check – none applicable).
- No pre-existing March rev-rec entries for either customer, so no duplication.
- No exceptions flagged; all amounts fully supported.

CHECKLIST
- US 'Revenue recognition' marked IN_PROGRESS (not complete): this memo covers only Dunmore Foods and Harlow Freight. Any other customer contracts in scope for March remain with the revenue accountant.

FOLLOW-UPS FOR CONTROLLER
- April: ensure Harlow Q1 invoice (expected USD 13,600) is booked Dr 1100 / Cr 1300, not to revenue.
- Dunmore analytics module release of USD 1,000/month continues Apr–Dec 2026 alongside the USD 4,000 core release.
